title: Time in the moving system, up to the same scale
spoken: The moving time is the same coefficient times t minus v x over c squared.
explanation: Requiring light to go at c in both directions in both systems fixes the time combination: t − vx/c², times the same factor as the position.
assumptions: The moving system k moves along the x axis of the stationary system K at speed v, with |v| < c, and the two origins coincide at time zero.
Modern teaching notation. The paper writes the moving system's coordinates as xi and tau, not x′ and t′, its gamma as beta, and the speed of light as V.

notes.title: A time that depends on place
notes.explanation: vx over c squared is a time: distant clocks in the moving system are set differently. This term is where simultaneity stops being shared.

notes.title: c squared
notes.explanation: Divided by the square of the speed of light, the correction is small for everyday v and x.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Once light's speed is the same both ways in both systems, only one number, the common factor, remains unknown.

notes.title: Times the same unknown factor
notes.explanation: The factor that multiplies the position equation.

notes.title: t corrected for position
notes.explanation: Subtracting that place-dependent time from t.

notes.title: Speed times position
notes.explanation: v times x: events farther along x get a larger correction.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: The paper's V. It enters because both systems must find the same speed for light.

notes.title: Position in the stationary system
notes.explanation: Where the event is along x, in the stationary system's coordinates.

notes.title: The factor not yet fixed
notes.explanation: The light conditions fix everything but this common scale. The paper carries it as phi(v) times beta and then shows phi(v) is 1.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: The speed of k relative to K. Its sign gives the direction.

notes.title: Time in the stationary system
notes.explanation: When the event happens, by the stationary system's synchronized clocks.

notes.title: Time in the moving system
notes.explanation: When the same event happens, by the moving system's synchronized clocks. The paper calls it tau; it is a coordinate, not the time one clock records.

sentence.text: The time in the moving system
